newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds-S.Koreans eye nearby soybeans/meal.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds-S.Koreans eye nearby soybeans/meal.

text.p: South Korean feed millers and crushers were seen eyeing nearby shipments of soybeans and soymeal this week following a sharp fall in prices in the world soybean market, traders said on Monday.
"We expect some buyers to jump into the market this week as current soybean prices are close to their target prices," a trader with a local feed miller in South Korea said.

The July soybean futures contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fell 3/4 cents to close at $8.35-1/2 a bushel. The contract hit a low on the Project A after-hours trading system in Asia of $8.21 a bushel.

The trader said other buyers were also waiting for the National Livestock Cooperatives Federation's (NLCF) to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal after it had passed on a tender last week due to high offer prices.

The NLCF was seeking 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for arrival by September 30 or October 20, 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet for November-December arrival and 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal for arrival in December.
The Korea Feed Association (KFA) bought 15,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal at $296.50 a tonne C&F from Andre last Thursday for August 20 arrival at the western port of Inchon.
In Japan, buyers are likely to remain sidelined this week, as old crop prices are still hovering at levels above that of new crop, traders said.
Japanese importers have already finished covering U.S. soybeans for July shipment.

"We may consider buying more U.S. soybean if the July (futures) contract falls to around $7.20 (a bushel) level. But given the current backwardation, we'll wait for new crop," a senior official of a major edible oil maker in Japan said.
